text:
incident-bot: ALERT: detected sustained route oscillation and increased packet loss on upstream transit provider CarrierZ affecting eu-west-1 and us-east-1 (Ashburn). Metric spike started ~1952467900. Auto-page to oncall.

maria: I'm on the page. Seeing 12-20% packet loss on pings to 198.51.100.0/24 from our eu-west edge. BGP updates show flapping to multiple as-paths. Service alerts for customers in EU (ingest + LLM inference) showing retries/timeouts.

kevin: Confirmed. Cloud egress counters show retransmits up ~5x. Provider-side implies short withdraws then re-announces with different prepends.

alex: Traceroute from ashburn-edge to upstream:
```
traceroute to 198.51.100.1 (198.51.100.1), 30 hops max
 1  ashburn-edge (10.1.1.2)  0.45 ms 0.37 ms 0.39 ms
 2  203.0.113.1  1.23 ms 1.19 ms 1.21 ms
 3  carrierz-gw (198.51.100.254)  20.8 ms 45.2 ms 22.1 ms
 4  198.51.100.1  *  *  *
```
Looks like the intermediate hop oscillates.

maria: Customer impact: some hosted-api traffic getting 504s and streaming connections drop after 10-20s. CS ticket queue has 8 customers reporting degraded latency.

sre-bot: Pager rotation: escalate to netops + open incident channel #inc-1952468000. Severity: HIGH (SRE-SEV2).

kevin: Can we shift pref to CarrierY for affected prefixes? We have an alternate transit in eu-west. Prep plan: 1) Raise localpref for routes learned from CarrierY 2) Withdraw 198.51.100.0/24 from CarrierZ if oscillation persists 3) Contact CarrierZ NOC with community tags and BGP dump.

networking-bot: Current BGP flap counts (last 15m): CarrierZ: 78 updates, CarrierY: 2 updates. AS path churn observed: +prepends and short AS path changes.

lisa: I'm taking incident lead for routing. I'll coordinate provider comms and net changes. @kevin please hold on config changes until I ack — want to avoid oscillation loops.

kevin: ack — prepping NetOps runbook snippets. If lisa gives go, we'll push a temporary policy: set localpref 200 for CarrierY for prefixes matching 198.51.100.0/24 via bird/externals. Example (bird):
```
route filter FILTER_TO_SHIFT {
  if net ~ 198.51.100.0/24 then accept;
  reject;
}
protocol static PREFER_CARRIERY {
  source bgp table master;
  export FILTER_TO_SHIFT;
  next hop self;
  local_pref 200;
}
```
Don't copy verbatim, testing in lab first.

maria: We should also flip health-checks to failover earlier: set ingress healthcheck threshold to 3 failed attempts for critical routes so traffic moves faster to healthy edge. Ops impact: some sticky sessions may drop.

lisa: On it. Opening ticket with CarrierZ NOC now, attaching BGP dumps + traceroutes. Email to noc@carrierz.example included. Reference ticket: CZ-INC-8672.

ops-support: Noted customer list: 8 mid-market customers seeing >30% errors; 3 enterprise customers in eu-west reporting heartbeat timeouts. We're prepping customer comms: PSAT will send "degraded performance" note in 15m if sustained.

kevin: Lab test of policy looks good. If we push prefer to CarrierY, traffic in eu-west should shift within 30s of BGP convergence. Risk: if CarrierY capacity hits rate limit, we may need to throttle large flows.

maria: Monitoring: create temporary dashboards for per-customer error-rate and per-edge packetloss. Also add Flow logs sampling increase for affected prefixes.

networking-bot: Route history snapshot for 198.51.100.0/24 (last 60m):
- 1952467200: stable via CarrierZ
- 1952467740: first withdraw
- 1952467896: reannounce with prepends
- 1952467950-1952468050: repeated withdraws/reannounces (~78 updates)

lisa: CarrierZ responded: "We're seeing internal flap between PoP-A and PoP-B, engineering investigating; no known DDoS." We asked for timeline and AS-path details.

maria: Decision: move ahead with soft pref shift to CarrierY for 198.51.100.0/24 in eu-west and ashburn for next 30m, monitor, then rollback if issues. If CarrierZ stabilizes, revert. Documenting change now.

kevin: Deploying change in 30s to eu-west routers only. Will watch bgp update rate and egress counters.

sre-bot: Change scheduled by kevin at 1952468030. Auto-notify on BGP update rate > 200/min or packet loss > 5% for 5m.

kevin: Change applied to eu-west. Observing convergence: traffic shift starting. BGP updates from CarrierY increased slightly as expected.

maria: Early metrics: client error rate down from 18% -> 6% in eu-west within 90s. Packet loss to 198.51.100.0/24 from eu-west edges down to 1-2%. Ashburn shows partial improvement.

lisa: Good. Notifying CarrierZ that we took a soft-pref action and asking for ETA. Asking them to provide root cause once fixed.

ops-support: Drafted customer note: "We detected packet loss on one upstream provider impacting traffic in EU and US-East. We've temporarily routed traffic via an alternate provider; service levels improving. We'll follow up with root cause." Asking for review.

maria: Handing incident to night oncall at 1952468120: @lisa hands off to @alex for overnight monitoring. Alex please acknowledge.

alex: Acknowledged. I'll monitor BGP updates, packetloss, and customer tickets. If CarrierZ reverts and updates reappear, will coordinate rollback.

lisa: Thanks Alex — I will keep CarrierZ ticket open and add timeline notes. Postmortem owner: lisa. Please collect config diffs, BGP dumps, and provider comms.

incident-bot: Incident status: mitigated (traffic shifted). Severity: HIGH -> monitoring. Incident channel archived in 2h unless reopened.

maria: Closing local triage. Action items:
- lisa: PM for postmortem + timeline
- kevin: save config change diff and automate canary for localpref shifts
- alex: overnight watch + escalate if flaps resume
- ops-support: final customer note once CarrierZ provides RCA

sre-bot: Logged incident ID: RI-2026-1952468000.

maria: Thanks all.
